title: The exact collision cost of low-weight uniformity for polynomial maps over GF(2)
description:
Let Q: F2n → F2n have coordinates of algebraic degree at most k, and suppose its output on a uniform input is d-wise uniform but Q is not a bijection. The smallest possible ordered-collision excess C(Q) − 2n is exactly 2max(⌈n/k⌉, d+1), for every k ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ d < n. For compressing maps F2n → F2m (m ≤ n) the minimum of C(Q) − 22n−m is 2max(2⌈n/k⌉ − m, ⌈n/k⌉, d+1).

Both lower bounds are classical (Delsarte's support bound and McEliece-type divisibility); the contribution is that the larger one is always attained, by an explicit ring of gates, and the exact answer for compressing maps.

Contents: the paper, a plain-language explainer, and a complete Lean 4 proof (no Mathlib, no sorry, standard axioms only) with a comparator-checked Challenge/Solution pair, plus independent Python checks. Run ./verify.sh to check everything.

New in version 2: Challenge/Solution comparator check, formalization.yaml, CI, citation metadata; the mathematics is unchanged. The paper is licensed CC BY 4.0; the code is MIT.
